domestic.debt_note: Finance Division's Debt Bulletin 1HFY-26 reports domestic debt at PKR55,363bn at Dec-25, up 1.6% in 1HFY26. The bulletin also reports a PKR2,926bn federal primary surplus in the first six months and interest expense of PKR3,563bn.
domestic.remittances: SBP reported workers' remittances of US$3.7bn in August 2026, up 16.5% YoY and 0.7% MoM; Jul-Aug FY27 inflows were US$7.3bn, up 14.7% YoY.
domestic.current_account: PM news reports the SBP Governor attributed reserve build-up to remittances and described the current-account deficit as the lowest; the exact latest balance figure is not verified in the available source.

global_read: Global tape is less stressed than last week: Brent is $101.16 (-2.61% 1d, +7.17% 1mo), WTI is $93.48 (-6.80% 1d, +7.37% 1mo), VIX is 14.85, and the S&P 500 is modestly higher. USD/PKR is 277.20 with a stronger dollar, while the georisk radar remains moderate at 54. Lower oil supports PSX sentiment, but the rupee and conflict channels keep the regime risk-off.
drivers: SBP kept the policy rate unchanged at 11.50% on 2026-09-14; the next scheduled MPC meeting is 2026-10-26. Source: https://www.sbp.org.pk/our-operations/monetary-policy

PBS reported August 2026 CPI inflation at 11.1% YoY versus 9.2% in July; urban and rural core inflation were 8.8% and 8.5%. Source: https://www.pbs.gov.pk/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Monthly-Review-August-2026.pdf

SBP reported total liquid FX reserves of US$23.7158bn as of 2026-09-04, and its latest displayed cutoffs include 11.8990% for the 6-month MTB and 12.3000% for the 10-year fixed PIB. Source: https://www.sbp.org.pk/cmd/index.htm

Finance Division's Debt Bulletin 1HFY-26 reports domestic debt of PKR55,363bn at Dec-25, a 1.6% 1HFY26 increase, and a PKR2,926bn federal primary surplus in the first six months. Source: https://www.finance.gov.pk/dpco/debt_bulletin_1hy_2026.pdf

IMF completed Pakistan's third EFF review and second RSF review on 2026-05-08, allowing about US$1.1bn under EFF and US$220m under RSF; the IMF schedule places the fourth EFF review on 2026-09-15. Sources: https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/05/08/pr-26147-pakistan-imf-completes-3rd-rev-of-extended-arrangement-under-eff-and-2nd-rev-arrang-rsf and https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2026/101/article-A001-en.xml

SBP reported August 2026 workers' remittances of US$3.7bn, up 16.5% YoY, with Jul-Aug FY27 inflows of US$7.3bn, up 14.7% YoY. Source: https://www.sbp.org.pk/assets/documents/press-release/PR-09-September-2026.pdf

PM news reports the SBP Governor credited remittances with reserve build-up and a low current-account deficit; the exact latest balance figure is not verified. Source: https://mettisglobal.news/PSXRoundup

PM news reports September 21's KSE-100 close at 171,153.16, up 268.58 points, while oil prices reached their lowest levels since September 10 on diplomacy hopes. Sources: https://www.brecorder.com/news/40440469/psx-buying-continues-kse-100-up-over-200-points and https://www.dawn.com/business

next_events.event: KSE-100 closed at 171,153.16 after a volatile positive session; oil and diplomacy remain the key external drivers.
Oil prices fell on diplomacy hopes, easing immediate supply concerns while leaving geopolitical risk unresolved.
